To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the BCS theory for superconductivity is not complete, and that the superconducting gap can be smaller or bigger than $\Delta_0$, depending on the asymmetry of the attraction band with respect to the Fermi energy, and the chemical potential can be different than the center of the band.

(i) there are two possible solutions of the gap equation, one of which corresponds to the BCS gap and the other one to the gap that is three times smaller than the BCS gap, and (ii) the BCS gap can be formed only if the chemical potential is close to the center of the interaction band.
(i) the superconducting state of a single-band s-wave superconductor is not unique, and (ii) there is an equilibrium state with a quasiparticles population imbalance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the low temperature limit (T=0) of the BCS model, with the assumption of a general asymmetric attractive potential, and the analysis of the equilibrium states of the superconductor.
the study of the equilibrium states of superconductors at zero temperature in the BCS approximation.
new equilibrium states of a superconductor in the low-temperature regime.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the superconducting state of the BCS model is not unique, and the BCS gap is only one of the two possible gaps.
the BCS theory is a theory of the superconducting phase transition, but not a theory of superconductivity.
the BCS gap is not a robust quantity, and its existence and value depend strongly on the position of the chemical potential with respect to the center of the interaction band.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a new type of equilibrium states in the standard BCS model.
the BCS model has a rich phenomenology, which was not explored before.
the superconductivity is not an all or nothing phenomenon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BCS theory, in its standard version, is not able to describe correctly the low temperature limit when the chemical potential is outside of the attraction band.
, if the chemical potential is shifted away from the center of the attractive interaction band, the energy gap is reduced.
the superconducting gap can be formed in the presence of quasiparticle imbalances, which are induced by the chemical potential being different from the center of the interaction band.
